steps.title: Know your models
steps.html:
In VR, type the gray word in Filter models.

@MODELS@

This list is also in VR: open your menu, click the Canvas tab, then pick our assignment.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. The steps are in Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Castle in Filter environments. Click Medieval Castle (Day), then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Build the floor
steps.html:
Walk to an open, flat spot. Open your menu (the top button on your right controller) and click Models.

@SKETCH@

Part A: lay down 1 Flat.

Part B: line up 4 Rods side by side. Push them against the back edge of the Flat, on its left side.

✋ Grab a model with the palm trigger. Keep every piece its real size.

steps.title: Write the area with models
steps.html:
How many small squares cover the whole floor? Find the area of each part. Then add.

In front of the floor, make a line of models: Part A's area, a Plus Sign, Part B's area, an Equal Sign, then the total.

🗣 Say it out loud: how did you find the area of each part?

steps.title: Extra, if you have time
steps.html: Slide the 4 Rods to a new spot along the Flat. They must still touch it. Does the floor need the same number of tiles? Why?

steps.title: Snap or record, then submit
steps.html:
Stand back so the floor and your answer both fit. Open your menu, click Library, then Camera.

Take a photo, or switch to Video and record up to 30 seconds.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your photo or video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

One photo or one video is the only thing you turn in.

🔁 Want to fix it? Move the models and submit a new one.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Open the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR? below.

vr.full: Your photo or video (30 seconds or less) shows the floor with 1 Flat and 4 Rods touching, and your answer in Number models: Part A's area + Part B's area = the total.

sketchbook.title: Tile the floor sketch
sketchbook.look: This is Leonardo's sketch of the floor. Each small square on the grid is 1 square unit. A Flat covers 100 small squares. A Rod covers 10.
sketchbook.do: Drag or tap the pieces onto the sketch, one part at a time. Then build your equation with the number tiles.

eq.do: Build an equation for the whole floor: Part A's area, +, Part B's area, =, the total. Tap a tile, or drag it to the line.
eq.noPlus: Show both parts. Put a + between Part A's area and Part B's area.
eq.notTrue: Your equation says {eq}. The two sides of the = do not match. Check your adding.
eq.wrongParts: Your equation says {eq}. Count the small squares in each part again.
eq.ok: Yes! Your equation shows both parts and the whole floor.

write.prompt:
A math paragraph tells how you solved it. Write 4 sentences or more (45 words or more):
  1. What did you build, and what is the answer?
  2. How did you solve it? Use the numbers.
  3. How do you know it is right?
  4. Use 2 of our math words.

checks.label: How you solved it, with numbers
How you know it is right

starters: I know it is right because

sketchbook.full: You tiled both parts and built a true equation for the whole floor. Your paragraph has 4 sentences, 45 words or more, and lights up every check.
